title: Repository validator regression-proofing governance
purpose: Define discovery-only validator regression-proofing expectations before future UI or app-surface work changes validator load, caching, or routing.

authorityBoundary.notes: This artifact records regression-proofing design only. Validators enforce USF semantics but do not invent platform meaning.

assuranceImpact: Validator optimisation can create false passes if path narrowing, parse reuse, cache reuse, or generated report reuse excludes correctness-affecting inputs.

Fail-closed behaviour must be preserved for unknown controlled values, stale reports, unknown evidence status, provider-mode mismatch, environment mismatch, planned-only schemas, missing evidence, and source-import ambiguity.
Generated reports remain lower authority and cannot replace raw evidence, semantic definitions, or validator checks.
safeOptions: Use explicit input manifests only after each manifest includes all semantic, schema, vocabulary, taxonomy, registry, evidence, fixture, and command inputs for the validator scope.
Use per-run parse caches only when cache keys include file path, content hash, lifecycle state where applicable, and strict parse error identity.
Use affected-validation routing only after planted-defect or selftest cases prove included and excluded path classes are correct.
Keep compatibility command aliases until command-surface governance authorises and validates any change.
unsafeShortcuts: Skipping generated or evidence directories without proving they are outside the validator scope.
Treating stale generated reports as pass evidence.
Reusing parsed JSON after file content changes inside a run.
Promoting planned schemas to active because a validator or report accepts them.
Removing planted defects or selftests to speed up validators.

validationProofExpectation: Each validator optimisation must include selftests or planted-defect cases for stale input, missing input, invalid JSON, unknown controlled value, generated-report non-authority, and omitted path classes where applicable.
Before and after comparisons must record the command surface, input manifest or scan scope, content hashes, pass or fail status, and any intentionally changed diagnostics.
A narrowed validator run must be compared against the corresponding full validator run for the selected scope before it can replace default routing.
Any unknown dependency, unclassified input, missing fixture, or stale cache condition must fail closed to the broader validation gate.

acceptanceCriteriaTrace.criterion: Proposal identifies candidate invariants, test cost, tooling options, and no-regression value.

criteria: Cache and partial-run risks are documented.

candidateInvariants.invariant: Unknown controlled vocabulary values fail closed.
candidateInvariants.generatorShape: Generate allowed values, aliases, unknown strings, empty strings, case variants, and structurally valid but non-canonical values.
candidateInvariants.pilotValue: Protects vocabulary validation from accepting aliases or unknown future values.

candidateInvariants.invariant: Taxonomy classifications remain unique and scoped to the intended taxonomy.
candidateInvariants.generatorShape: Generate duplicate IDs, cross-taxonomy IDs, missing IDs, and valid scoped IDs.
candidateInvariants.pilotValue: Protects taxonomy catalogue uniqueness and scope assumptions.

candidateInvariants.invariant: Schema registry lifecycle state does not become active without file and validator-checkable support.
candidateInvariants.generatorShape: Generate planned, missing-file, invalid-file, active-with-file, and active-without-validator states.
candidateInvariants.pilotValue: Protects schema activation safeguards before future contract or UI work.

candidateInvariants.invariant: Generated reports cannot satisfy raw evidence or semantic authority requirements.
candidateInvariants.generatorShape: Generate proof claims backed by raw evidence, generated reports only, stale reports, unknown status, and missing evidence references.
candidateInvariants.pilotValue: Protects authority order and fail-closed proof validation.

candidateInvariants.invariant: Provider mode and environment do not upgrade each other by implication.
candidateInvariants.generatorShape: Generate hermetic mock, live external provider, production shaped, production live, and mismatched combinations.
candidateInvariants.pilotValue: Protects provider/environment separation before app-surface proof expansion.

testCostModel: Start with bounded deterministic seeds and small generated case counts per invariant.
Run property pilots behind an explicit validator selftest or assurance command until runtime cost is measured.
Keep planted-defect fixtures as non-negotiable regression coverage; properties supplement rather than replace fixtures.
Fail property runs on flakiness, seed nondeterminism, unbounded shrinking, or runtime budget breach.

toolingOptions.option: Use existing test runner with hand-rolled deterministic generators.
toolingOptions.dependencyImpact: No dependency addition required for a pilot.
toolingOptions.risk: Less shrink support; generator quality depends on local discipline.

toolingOptions.option: Adopt a property-testing library only after an approved dependency decision.
toolingOptions.dependencyImpact: Requires dependency, lockfile, supply-chain, and runtime-cost review.
toolingOptions.risk: Additional dependency and potential flakiness if not seed-bounded.

toolingOptions.option: Use schema or vocabulary fixture expansion instead of a library for catalogue invariants.
toolingOptions.dependencyImpact: No dependency addition, but more fixtures to maintain.
toolingOptions.risk: Can become fixture explosion if not risk-ranked.

noRegressionValue: Broadens validator assurance beyond known planted defects while retaining fail-closed fixture coverage.
Exposes acceptance of aliases, unknown values, missing evidence, stale reports, and lifecycle mismatches before UI work increases validator scope.
Creates measurable pilot cases for future validator optimisation without changing default validator routing now.
futureImplementationRequirements: Record deterministic seed, generated case count, shrink behaviour, runtime budget, and invariant owner.
Keep property tests isolated from semantic authority changes and dependency decisions.
Add failing fixture or planted-defect equivalents for any property-discovered regression before relying on it as a gate.

validatorSuiteImprovementMatrix.scope: Discovery/design only for validator-suite child issues. This matrix does not create shared libraries, validators, tests, commands, schemas, report schemas, or implementation code.

dependencyGraphDesign.state: Validator directories, planted-defect directories, validation package scripts, and command-surface references are inspected through observedValidatorState and related source references.
dependencyGraphDesign.assuranceImpact: A dependency graph prevents unsafe partial runs and cache reuse by requiring every validator input and generated-output boundary to be explicit.
dependencyGraphDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future graph implementation must compare full and graph-selected validator membership, run relevant selftests, and fail closed on unknown or unclassified dependencies.

commonLibraryExtractionDesign.state: Repeated concerns include strict JSON parsing, file scanning, controlled-value handling, report envelopes, and planted-defect resolution.
commonLibraryExtractionDesign.assuranceImpact: Shared utilities can reduce drift, but an unsafe extraction can centralise a false-pass bug across validators.
commonLibraryExtractionDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future extraction requires before-and-after validator equivalence, planted defects for shared failure modes, and unchanged diagnostics unless intentionally documented.

performanceProfilingDesign.state: Repository performance profiling evidence exists separately and identifies measured command timings and deferred profiling gaps.
performanceProfilingDesign.assuranceImpact: Performance work must not narrow validator scope without proving equivalence against correctness-affecting inputs.
performanceProfilingDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future profiling must record command, duration, memory where available, input classes, and no-regression cases before optimisation.

parallelExecutionDesign.state: Safe parallelisation must consider shared resources including generated reports, evidence directories, service state, ports, and cache files.
parallelExecutionDesign.assuranceImpact: Parallel runs can reduce feedback time but can corrupt outputs or hide ordering dependencies if shared resources are not isolated.
parallelExecutionDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future parallel execution requires declared resource locks, deterministic output paths, before-and-after command equivalence, and planted defects for race-sensitive checks where applicable.
dependencies: repository performance profiling governance safe parallelisation design

jsonOutputStandardDesign.state: Validators and reports need consistent machine-readable result envelopes without treating generated reports as semantic authority.
jsonOutputStandardDesign.assuranceImpact: Consistent JSON output improves aggregation and agent review, but schema-like output contracts must not be invented as active schemas without registry and validator support.
jsonOutputStandardDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future JSON output standard must parse strictly, distinguish raw evidence from generated reports, preserve exit-code semantics, and include negative fixtures for malformed or stale output.

reportSchemaStandardDesign.state: Validator report structure needs shape governance before aggregate or generated report consumers rely on it.
reportSchemaStandardDesign.assuranceImpact: A report schema can improve consistency, but marking a planned schema active without file and validator support would violate schema rules.
reportSchemaStandardDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future report schema work must consult the schema registry, parse strict JSON Schema, remain validator-checkable, and preserve raw evidence links.

selftestConsistencyDesign.state: Observed planted-defect directories show broad but uneven selftest fixture placement across validator families.
selftestConsistencyDesign.assuranceImpact: Consistent selftests protect validator optimisation from weakening fail-closed behaviour.
selftestConsistencyDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future selftest consistency work must keep planted defects, invalid JSON, stale evidence, unknown controlled values, and omitted path-class cases runnable by owning validators.

falsePositiveNegativeReviewDesign.state: Known risk classes include stale cache, unknown values, generated report overtrust, missing evidence, provider/environment mismatch, and narrowed path scans.
falsePositiveNegativeReviewDesign.assuranceImpact: False positives create noisy blockers while false negatives undermine USF authority and proof claims; false negatives are higher severity for fail-closed validators.
falsePositiveNegativeReviewDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future review must classify each validator rule by false-positive and false-negative risk and include negative controls for high-risk false negatives.

severityModelDesign.state: Validator outcomes need explicit blocking semantics for strict errors, warnings, informational findings, stale evidence, and unknown status.
severityModelDesign.assuranceImpact: Ambiguous severity can convert unknown or stale evidence into accidental pass evidence.
severityModelDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future severity model must fail closed on unknown status, stale reports, missing evidence, and authority conflicts, with selftests for each severity class.

documentationHelpOutputDesign.state: Validator command surfaces are exposed through package scripts, Make targets, workflows, and tool directories.
documentationHelpOutputDesign.assuranceImpact: Help output can improve agent use but must not overclaim readiness, production, staging, compliance, or provider proof scope.
documentationHelpOutputDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future help output must list scope, inputs, outputs, side effects, proof/environment relevance, generated-report boundaries, and compatibility aliases.

cacheabilityInputHashingDesign.state: Potential cache inputs include validator source, package scripts, Make targets, catalogues, registries, schemas, semantic instances, evidence manifests, generated report source manifests, fixtures, and command environment dimensions.
cacheabilityInputHashingDesign.assuranceImpact: Cache reuse can reduce repeated work but stale or under-hashed inputs can hide drift and create false passes.
cacheabilityInputHashingDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future cache work must include content hashes, lifecycle state, provider/environment dimensions, command identity, invalidation fixtures, and fallback to full validation on ambiguity.

partialRunSupportDesign.state: Partial-run support depends on a complete dependency graph, cache-safe hashing, and declared path-to-validator ownership.
partialRunSupportDesign.assuranceImpact: Affected-only validation can improve feedback but is unsafe unless excluded inputs are proven irrelevant for the selected validator scope.
partialRunSupportDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future partial runs must compare selected runs with full runs, include included and excluded path-class tests, and fail closed to full validation on unknown ownership.

staleEvidenceDetectionDesign.state: USF safety rules require stale, unknown, and missing evidence to fail closed and generated reports to remain lower authority.
staleEvidenceDetectionDesign.assuranceImpact: Stale evidence detection protects readiness and proof claims from being upgraded by old reports or missing raw evidence.
staleEvidenceDetectionDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future stale-evidence checks must test stale report status, unknown status, missing raw evidence, provider-mode mismatch, environment mismatch, and generated-report-only proof claims.

ruleToAuthorityTraceabilityDesign.state: Validator rules should trace to semantic definitions, ADRs, validator rule authority, runtime proof evidence expectations, or source implementation constraints as applicable.
ruleToAuthorityTraceabilityDesign.assuranceImpact: Traceability prevents validators from inventing semantics and helps reviewers distinguish rule enforcement from product meaning.
ruleToAuthorityTraceabilityDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future traceability work must fail unknown authority references closed and keep generated reports lower than semantic definitions and validator rules.

ruleToLinearIssueTraceabilityDesign.state: Linear tracks work only and is not USF authority; traceability to Linear can support backlog management but cannot define validator semantics.
ruleToLinearIssueTraceabilityDesign.assuranceImpact: Rule-to-issue links help manage work, but overusing Linear links can confuse operational tracking with semantic authority.
ruleToLinearIssueTraceabilityDesign.validationProofExpectation: Future rule-to-issue traceability must keep repository authority references primary, treat Linear links as operational context, and avoid closing issues without acceptance evidence.

parentValidatorSuiteImprovementClosure.childStatusObservation: Linear child issue check for USF-355 showed all children completed after USF-995 closure.

validatorInventoryComplete.basis: observedValidatorState records validator directories, planted-defect directories, fixture directories, manifest directories, and validation-relevant package scripts, with USF-505 completed as the inventory baseline.
validatorInventoryComplete.residualGap: Future implementation may add richer machine-readable inventories, but parent planning inventory criteria are satisfied for discovery closure.

ruleToAuthorityTraceabilityGaps: Rule-to-authority references need primary links to USF semantic definitions, ADRs, validator rules, runtime proof evidence expectations, or source implementation constraints, not Linear alone.
Generated reports must remain lower authority in any validator output or aggregate summary.
Unknown authority references, missing source contracts, and planned-only schema references must fail closed in future traceability validators.
cacheAndPartialRunRisks: Under-hashed inputs can hide semantic, schema, evidence, fixture, generated-output, package-script, or command-surface drift.
Affected-only validation can exclude correctness-affecting inputs unless a complete dependency graph and path ownership model exist.
Stale parse caches, generated reports, and aggregate summaries can produce false pass evidence if not invalidated by content hash and lifecycle state.
Unknown ownership or missing hashes must fall back to broader validation.
uiBlockingValidatorGaps: Generated-client contract and lifecycle validation before UI consumption.
App-surface proof routing validation for provider mode and environment separation.
Aggregate command manifest coverage before new aggregate validator routing.
Before-and-after validator equivalence for any optimisation or refactor.
Stale evidence and generated-report non-authority detection.
parentNonClaims: No cache or partial-run mechanism was implemented.
No UI readiness claim was made.
